A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FeatureTracker/CV-RNN study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including v3's final supplementary figure sheet.

before.justification: v1 reports original shell-game experiments, FeatureTracker model evaluations, human behavioral results, ablations and generalization analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds comparison-model outcomes and experiments with backgrounds, textures and disappearing distractors.

M1.justification: The CV-RNN's complex-valued attention, recurrent state, phase initialization and combined classification/synchrony objective are retained. Sections 3–4, Appendices A.6–A.8 and the architecture tables describe the same proposed procedures.

E1.justification: A.12.2–A.12.3 add substantially different input conditions: changing colored backgrounds, textured objects, distractors entering/leaving the frame and distractors vanishing. Existing shell-game, color/shape, irregular-trajectory and target-occlusion scenarios remain; the disappearing-object changes apply only to distractors.

E2.justification: A.11.1 adds VideoMAE to the FeatureTracker comparisons in Fig. A.14, reports attempted DINO feature-extractor baselines with MLP/RNN readouts, and adds a separate SAM2 evaluation. These expand the evaluated alternatives beyond v1's supervised transformer, CNN and recurrent comparisons. RNN-L and full-colorspace pretraining controls already existed.

E3.justification: A.12.3 adds a cross-condition design using models trained with always-visible distractors and models trained with distractors entering/leaving the frame. A.11.1 introduces SAM2 evaluation initialized from the target mask, using IoU > 0.9 on a stated 1,000 images. This differs from binary-video accuracy; the original training and human-study protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test robustness to background dynamics, texture and changes in distractor presence, including a retraining control for entering/leaving distractors (Figs. A.17–A.19). These substantially extend the questions tested. The original phase ablations, parameter controls, irregular-trajectory analyses and target-occlusion tests are retained.

E5.justification: Five shell-game initializations with standard errors (Fig. A.1), benchmark 95% confidence intervals (Fig. 5), and human binomial tests (A.10.2) remain unchanged. Added results, including SAM2's undefined ± term, do not document a new repetition count or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds VideoMAE scores, DINO nonconvergence and SAM2's reported 0.001875% (±7.65e−05), alongside extensive new robustness results. CV-RNN has the highest plotted mean accuracies in Figs. A.17–A.19. These are additional results under new conditions, not improved scores on the original experiments. SAM2's aggregation and percentage scale remain unclear.

T1.justification: The circuit equations, complex-operation definitions, synchrony-loss derivation and error-consistency equations are substantively unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal assumption is introduced; SAM2's overlap threshold is an evaluation criterion.

C1.justification: Both versions present FeatureTracker and CV-RNN as a computational proof of concept for synchrony-based tracking, claiming stronger generalization and closer human behavior than the tested alternatives. The shortened abstract and added supporting experiments retain these central contributions and claims.

C2.justification: A.11.1 newly interprets VideoMAE's weak performance as suggesting architecture matters more than training procedure. A.12.3 discusses robustness and transfer under disappearing distractors. Conversely, A.2 removes the explicit computational-expense and unmatched-operations limitation, while retaining the other principal limitations.

D1.justification: v3 specifies VideoMAE's ViT-S/patch-16 configuration and pretraining, DINO's initialization/readouts, SAM2-tiny's prompting, and generation rules for the added scenarios. It replaces the anonymous code/data link with a named GitHub repository. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware and training-time disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Astrand, Lee, Cai, Caron and Ravi, covering target selection, complex networks, future tracking benchmarks and new comparators. It removes the Bongard-LOGO, cABC, SVRT and PSVRT examples and associated citations. The central positioning relative to PathTracker and earlier synchrony models remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive limited copyediting, related-work examples are shortened, and contact/funding text changes. An appendix list of figures and new experimental subsections are added, but most prose and the overall narrative organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual evidence with multi-condition plots for VideoMAE, backgrounds, textures and disappearing distractors. It adds a final explanatory/summary figure sheet, adds a legend to Fig. A.10, and resizes or relocates retained displays. Earlier trajectory, occlusion and error-consistency figures are preserved under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The new background, texture and distractor-presence experiments strengthen robustness evidence beyond v1's original scenarios, and VideoMAE broadens the comparisons. These provide a limited net quality gain. Real-video scalability remains untested, while SAM2's unclear percentage/aggregation and the removal of the computational-cost limitation weaken reporting and temper the improvement.
